label: 28 Oct 1528, fr. 3077 no. 23
sample_original: Je tiens de bon lieu que la royne a dict a quelqung a prive que, se faisant, l'Empereur ne cessera jamais qu'il n'ayt ruine le roy d'Angleterre
sample_en: I have it from a good source that the Queen told someone in private that, if it goes ahead, the Emperor will never cease until he has ruined the King of England.
why: Fetched the archive.org full text of Bourrilly and de Vaissiere: the whole letter is printed as continuous 16th-century French with the deciphered passages included (italics lost in the OCR, words present); it parses and translates throughout, with only OCR noise and bracketed editorial restorations.

label: no. 94, ff. 120r-121r, viceroy of Sicily to Ferdinand, Messina, 27 Apr 1503
file: esp318no94/ct94_brackx.txt; GitHub issue #62 body (gh): interlinear decipherment and READING.md v3
sample_original: Y COMO ESTO PASSEMOS EN ANOCHECIENDO, [nap] primeros [que] entraron ... DESPUES, A LA MEDIA NOCHE, COMENZARON D'ENTRAR infantes [y] saquearon [la] ...
sample_en: AND WE PASSED THIS AT NIGHTFALL, ... the first who entered ... afterwards, AT MIDNIGHT, INFANTRY BEGAN TO ENTER and sacked the ... (holes remain)
why: Brackx's provisional reading (issue #62) is Spanish with the clear passages intact, but about 90 code groups are open and most sentences carry '...' or [xxx] holes; the gist (Seminara, the sack, prisoners, Portocarrero's death) is recoverable but few sentences are complete. The repository file itself holds only the sign transcription.

label: Esp. 318 no. 5, Federico III to the Catholic Monarchs, 11 Jan 1497
sample_original: Da poi de havere resposto ad micer Joan Scriva, oratore de le Maiestate Vostre, circa quanto da parte de quelle me havea declarato del matrimonio de una de le vostrea infante
sample_en: After replying to Messer Joan Escriva, your Majesties' orator, about what he declared on your behalf concerning the marriage of one of your infantas ...
why: Parisi prints the whole letter in the appendix as continuous Neapolitan-flavoured Italian with editorial brackets for restored letters; short, fully coherent and easy to translate.

label: R4332 (= R3816), Heusner to Oxenstierna, Kassel 15 May 1637
file: Kopal's blog post of 30 Aug 2024 on kopaldev.de (unedited German decipherment); doi 10.58009/aere-perennius0116 unreachable
sample_original: Wiewohl ich nun vermeinet, dessen orts DIE ALTE DEUOTION GEGEN DIE CRON ZU FINDEN. So erfahre ich aber das HERR UND KNECHT SEHR GEENDERT UND AM GANZEN HOFE AUSSER DER 503. NICHTT EINER MEHR UFFRECHT SCHWEDISCH
sample_en: Although I had thought to find the old devotion to the Crown in this place, I learn that master and servant have greatly changed and at the whole court, apart from 503, not one is any longer upright Swedish.
why: The blog gives the full German decipherment with the cipher parts in capitals; most sentences read and translate, but 3-digit nomenclature numbers (503, 628, 764, 147, 571 ...) stand for unread names and some transcription slips remain.

label: Cox to Milroy, 3 Dec 1862 (Richard Bean decipherment)
sample_original: China quest whether transportation in reach what is if bully imboden ly to forward ...
sample_en: If your information as to Imboden is confirmed, let me know [by] what route you shall try to reach him, also [how] far forward in the Moorefield Road your [present] transportation will supply your [force] ...
why: The repository transcription is the scrambled route-cipher word grid, but Tomokiyo's page gives Bean's full plaintext as two squares of clear English with a few bracketed corrections; it reads as a complete telegram.
